questions.question: only_box2a
questions.v86_text: Is it true that you had no capital gains in 2025 other than capital gain distributions in box 2a of Form 1099-DIV (for example, no gain from selling stock, funds or other property)?
questions.v87_text: Is it true that you had no capital gains in 2025 other than capital gain distributions in box 2a of Form 1099-DIV, and that you had no sale in 2025 of stock, bonds, funds or other property that you must report on Form 8949 or Schedule D (even one with no gain or loss)? Sales inside an IRA or 401(k) and losses on personal items do not count.

v86.exception1.only-box2a-capital-gains: Exception 1 component C1 (ADR-0050): whether the return's only capital gains are Form 1099-DIV box-2a capital-gain distributions. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession. Distinct from the checked schedule-d-required.conclusion.
v86.sli-scope.not-claimed-as-dependent: Student Loan Interest Deduction eligibility component (legal zero, not a block): the filer is not claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer (Pub. 970 p.33, Example 2: "neither you nor your parents may deduct the student loan interest"). Filer-level. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default. yes asserts the filer is not claimed as a dependent and the route proceeds; no asserts the filer IS claimed as a dependent -- the law's own definite $0 for this return, not missing information and not a block.
v86.taxpayer-over-65: Taxpayer is over 65 years of age for 2025
v86.spouse-over-65: Spouse is over 65 years of age for 2025

v87.exception1.only-box2a-capital-gains: Exception 1 component C1 (ADR-0050): whether the return's only capital gains are Form 1099-DIV box-2a capital-gain distributions and the filer had no 2025 sale of stock, bonds, funds or other property that must be reported on Form 8949 or Schedule D, including one with no gain or loss; sales inside an IRA or 401(k) and losses on personal-use property do not count (Form 1040 instructions, line 7a: "If you sold a capital asset ... you must complete and attach Form 8949 and Schedule D"; Schedule D instructions, Capital Assets Held for Personal Use: "Loss from the sale or exchange of a capital asset held for personal use isn't deductible"). Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default, presence-before-value, free supersession. Distinct from the checked schedule-d-required.conclusion.
v87.sli-scope.not-claimed-as-dependent: Student Loan Interest Deduction eligibility component (legal zero, not a block): neither the filer nor, on a joint return, the filer's spouse is claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's 2025 return (Form 1040 instructions, Schedule 1 line 21: "You, or your spouse if filing jointly, aren't claimed as a dependent on someone else's ... 2025 tax return"; Pub. 970 p.33). An actual claim, not whether someone could claim. Filer-level. Contributed categorical assertion, domain {yes, no}, no default. yes asserts neither is claimed and the route proceeds; no asserts the filer or, on a joint return, the spouse IS claimed -- the law's own definite $0 for this return, not missing information and not a block.
v87.taxpayer-over-65: Taxpayer was born before January 2, 1961. A person reaches age 65 on the day before the 65th birthday. A taxpayer who was born before January 2, 1961 but died in 2025 before reaching age 65 is not included.
v87.taxpayer-blind: Taxpayer was totally blind as of December 31, 2025, or has a statement certified by an eye doctor that the taxpayer cannot see better than 20/200 in the better eye with glasses or contact lenses, or that the field of vision is 20 degrees or less.
v87.spouse-over-65: Spouse was born before January 2, 1961. A person reaches age 65 on the day before the 65th birthday. A spouse who was born before January 2, 1961 but died in 2025 before reaching age 65 is not included.
v87.spouse-blind: Spouse was totally blind as of December 31, 2025, or has a statement certified by an eye doctor that the spouse cannot see better than 20/200 in the better eye with glasses or contact lenses, or that the field of vision is 20 degrees or less.
